market.title: Machine learning toolkit can improve odds of drug development success
market.summary: Southwest Research Institute developed GAMES, a generative AI tool using large language models to generate chemical structures for drug development. The tool identified 18 antiviral candidates for filovirus infections, with recommendations in the top 10% of ranked candidates. The team plans to use reinforcement learning from human feedback to improve the output.

market.title: Mol2Image turns drug molecular descriptors into images to predict
market.summary: Researchers published in BMC Bioinformatics a deep learning framework, Mol2Image, that converts drug molecular descriptors and Morgan fingerprints into 64-by-64 grayscale images and uses a lightweight convolutional neural network to predict drug–drug interactions. It achieved 0.9608 accuracy on DrugBank and 0.9683 on ChCh-Miner, outperforming competitors including StructNet-DDI, while requiring only 21 descriptors.

market.title: Senior Machine Learning Research Scientist (m/f/d) - Generative AI for Drug Design - Pfizer
market.summary: Pfizer is hiring a Senior Machine Learning Research Scientist in Berlin to develop generative AI models for drug design. The role involves designing, implementing, and validating state-of-the-art machine learning tools for molecular and ligand-based drug discovery, with a focus on diffusion and flow-based approaches. The position is open to candidates with advanced degrees and experience in deep learning and cheminformatics.

market.title: LLNL’s Brase discusses advances by ATOM in accelerating drug discovery pipeline
market.summary: ATOM consortium co-lead Jim Brase said at a webinar that high-performance computing and machine learning have accelerated drug discovery, with generative design and molecular optimization demonstrated. The consortium, founded in 2017, has over a dozen members and is transitioning into a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. Brase noted future focus on active learning and adding biological features to models.

market.title: Adaption Labs Introduces ‘Invent a Dataset’: Training Data Generated From a Task Description, Not a Seed Corpus
market.summary: Adaption Labs released Invent a Dataset, a feature that generates structured training data from a task description without a seed corpus. The API supports instruction and preference pairs, with outputs in JSONL, JSON, CSV, or Parquet, and integrates with AutoScientist for co-optimization. AutoScientist reportedly beats manually configured training by 35% average.
